review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting native-speaker review. House style: moderate Bokmål with three genders (ei/-a for feminine nouns, en/-en masculine, et/-et neuter), weak past in -et, neuter definite plural in -ene, sju and tjue, "ble", "ga". Indirect speech in narration (spurte om han hadde ..., svarte at han ...), the perfect and past perfect, "hvis"-clauses. Sam goes to the interview and is offered the position.

english.source: drafted with the text; not reviewed

sentences.text: På mandag stod Sam opp tidlig. Han spiste litt brød, men han var ikke sulten.
sentences.english: On Monday Sam got up early. He ate a little bread, but he was not hungry.

sentences.text: Han var i sentrum en time for tidlig. Han gikk en tur i byen, og han ba en bønn: «Gud, hjelp meg å være ærlig.» Så gikk han til bokhandelen.
sentences.english: He was in the town centre an hour too early. He went for a walk in the town, and he said a prayer: "God, help me to be honest." Then he went to the bookshop.

sentences.text: Sjefen satt ved bordet og leste i en bok. «God dag,» sa han. «Du må være Sam. Kom inn.»
sentences.english: The manager sat by the table and read in a book. "Good day," he said. "You must be Sam. Come in."

sentences.text: De satte seg i et lite rom i butikken. Sjefen spurte om Sam hadde jobbet i en bokhandel før.
sentences.english: They sat down in a small room in the shop. The manager asked whether Sam had worked in a bookshop before.

sentences.text: Sam svarte at han ikke hadde det, men at han hadde lært mye norsk, og at han var glad i bøker. Han sa også at han ikke hadde noen erfaring, men at han ville lære.
sentences.english: Sam answered that he had not, but that he had learned a lot of Norwegian, and that he was fond of books. He also said that he had no experience, but that he wanted to learn.

sentences.text: Sjefen sa at det var et ærlig svar. «Jeg liker det,» sa han.
sentences.english: The manager said that it was an honest answer. "I like that," he said.

sentences.text: Hva gjør du hvis en kunde spør om en bok som du ikke kjenner?
sentences.english: What do you do if a customer asks about a book that you do not know?
sentences.speaker: sjef

sentences.text: Jeg sier at jeg ikke kjenner den. Men jeg skal spørre noen som vet.
sentences.english: I say that I do not know it. But I will ask someone who knows.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Bra. Og hvis du ikke forstår hva kunden sier?
sentences.english: Good. And if you do not understand what the customer says?
sentences.speaker: sjef

sentences.text: Da spør jeg en gang til. Det er ikke vanskelig å spørre.
sentences.english: Then I ask once more. It is not difficult to ask.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Det er riktig. Den som spør, lærer.
sentences.english: That is right. Whoever asks, learns.
sentences.speaker: sjef

sentences.text: Så fortalte sjefen om arbeidet. Det var ikke bare å selge bøker. De måtte også rydde bøkene og hjelpe kundene med å finne det de ville ha.
sentences.english: Then the manager told about the work. It was not only selling books. They also had to tidy the books and help the customers find what they wanted.

sentences.text: Stillingen er på deltid. Du må jobbe tre dager i uka, og annenhver helg.
sentences.english: The position is part-time. You must work three days a week, and every other weekend.
sentences.speaker: sjef

sentences.text: Deltid er bra for meg. Jeg går på skolen to dager i uka. Og annenhver helg går bra også.
sentences.english: Part-time is good for me. I go to school two days a week. And every other weekend is fine too.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Hva blir lønnen?
sentences.english: What will the pay be?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Lønnen er ikke stor, men du får lære mye. Og du får gode kollegaer.
sentences.english: The pay is not big, but you will learn a lot. And you will get good colleagues.
sentences.speaker: sjef

sentences.text: Hvem er kollegaene mine?
sentences.english: Who are my colleagues?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Du treffer dem på mandag. De er snille, og de liker arbeidet sitt.
sentences.english: You will meet them on Monday. They are kind, and they like their work.
sentences.speaker: sjef

sentences.text: Sam tenkte at arbeidet var mer enn han hadde trodd. Men han likte det han hørte.
sentences.english: Sam thought that the work was more than he had believed. But he liked what he heard.

sentences.text: Jeg har snakket med alle som har søkt. Du hadde ikke så mye erfaring, men du var ærlig, og det liker jeg.
sentences.english: I have spoken with everyone who has applied. You did not have so much experience, but you were honest, and I like that.
sentences.speaker: sjef

sentences.text: Vi vil gjerne tilby deg stillingen. Kan du begynne neste mandag?
sentences.english: We would like to offer you the position. Can you start next Monday?
sentences.speaker: sjef

sentences.text: Sam kunne nesten ikke tro det. «Ja,» sa han. «Takk for at dere tilbyr meg stillingen! Det vil jeg gjerne.»
sentences.english: Sam could hardly believe it. "Yes," he said. "Thank you for offering me the position! I would like that very much."

sentences.text: Han gikk ut av bokhandelen og ringte til Anna. «Sjefen har tilbudt meg stillingen! Jeg skal jobbe tre dager i uka og annenhver helg.»
sentences.english: He went out of the bookshop and called Anna. "The manager has offered me the position! I will work three days a week and every other weekend."

sentences.text: «Gratulerer!» sa hun. «Det visste jeg! Deltid er riktig for deg. Hvem er kollegaene dine?» «Det vet jeg ikke ennå,» svarte han.
sentences.english: "Congratulations!" she said. "I knew it! Part-time is right for you. Who are your colleagues?" "I do not know yet," he answered.

sentences.text: Om kvelden spiste de taco, selv om det var mandag. Nils spurte om han fikk smake på bøkene, og alle lo.
sentences.english: In the evening they ate tacos, even though it was Monday. Nils asked whether he could taste the books, and everyone laughed.

sentences.text: Før han sov, ba Sam: «Takk, Gud, for at jeg fikk tilbudet. Hjelp meg å gjøre arbeidet godt.»
sentences.english: Before he slept, Sam prayed: "Thank you, God, that I got the offer. Help me to do the work well."

sentences.text: Han hadde aldri vært så glad for en lønn han ikke hadde fått ennå.
sentences.english: He had never been so glad about pay that he had not yet received.

sentences.text: Marta ringte og ville invitere Sam til middag. «Du burde komme hit etter jobben,» sa hun, «så kan vi gå en tur i naturen.»
sentences.english: Marta called and wanted to invite Sam to dinner. "You ought to come here after work," she said, "and then we can go for a walk in nature."

sentences.text: Da han kom hjem, var han ikke alene: Anna og Lars ventet. Han hadde søkt, og nå hadde han en jobb.
sentences.english: When he came home, he was not alone: Anna and Lars were waiting. He had applied, and now he had a job.

sentences.text: Nå hadde han flere venner enn før, og han kunne snakke med dem på norsk.
sentences.english: Now he had more friends than before, and he could talk with them in Norwegian.
